```{=html}
<p id="welcome" class="unnumbered" style="font-size: 2rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; margin: 1.1rem 0 1rem;">Welcome</p>

<div class="abstract-section">
  <div class="abstract-content">
    <p><strong>This is a working sketch, not a published volume.</strong> The first two books moved capability into the model and then into the fleet. This one asks what changes when capability moves into <em>inference-time compute</em>: when a system spends compute at runtime, through loops, search, self-correction, and actions on the world, rather than only at training time. That shift is what "agentic" names once the framework noise is stripped away. The wager of this book is that the systems substrate beneath autonomous agents, the control loop, the management of state and memory, the typed interface to tools and environments, the orchestration of many stochastic nodes, the economics and reliability of multi-step inference, has settled enough to teach as fundamentals, while being honest that evaluation and the memory architecture remain open frontiers. If that wager fails the test, this introduction will read like a tour of today's tools, and the book waits.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

<p id="what-you-will-learn" class="unnumbered" style="font-size: 1.45rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.25; margin: 1.5rem 0 0.75rem;">What You Will Learn</p>

This book extends the foundations into systems that *act*, through four parts that move from the thesis to the substrate to the consequences:

- **Part I: The Inference-Time Frontier**: Establish why a third volume exists. The shift from training-time to inference-time compute, the control loop as the durable structure beneath any agent, and the nascent laws of spending compute at runtime.
- **Part II: The Substrate**: The durable engineering layer. State and memory as a memory-hierarchy problem, tools and environments as typed action surfaces, and orchestration as distributed systems with stochastic nodes.
- **Part III: Reliability and Economics**: The quantifiable properties of acting systems. How error compounds over a trajectory, what multi-step inference costs, and why evaluating a trajectory-shaped output is still an open problem.
- **Part IV: The Responsible Agent**: Governing systems that act. Containment and human oversight, the new attack surface opened by the action boundary, and the durable core that survives once the trends pass.

<p id="prerequisites" class="unnumbered" style="font-size: 1.45rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.25; margin: 1.5rem 0 0.75rem;">Prerequisites</p>

This book assumes:

- The foundations of *Introduction to Machine Learning Systems* (single-system ML engineering)
- The scale foundations of *Machine Learning Systems at Scale* (distributed training, serving, and inference economics)
- **Programming proficiency** in Python
- **Mathematics foundations** in linear algebra, probability, and the basics of control and search

<p id="a-note-on-durability" class="unnumbered" style="font-size: 1.45rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.25; margin: 1.5rem 0 0.75rem;">A Note on Durability</p>

This volume is written under a hard rule: no framework, product, or single-year benchmark appears in the body. Where the substrate is settled, it is taught as fundamentals; where it is not, the open problem is named as an open problem. That discipline is the reason this book can be written now without dating in two years, and it is also the reason some chapters deliberately stop at "here is the question" rather than pretending at "here is the answer."

:::
